Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-1-prompt-long-0128", "row_sha256": "ba760e0d7e803c2f6c6435c1eb8c5eb77e179c95dde93c394a62dc34f4d2e6e3", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "
hey, can you help me put together the material for the Maple Row Seed Exchange? the event is at Eastbank Community Hall on october 12, from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. Lena Ortiz and Dev Shah are organizing it, and the packet table will be near the hall entrance. i need a printable sign for the table, not a general event announcement or a social media post. The sign is meant for people who are already at the exchange and are deciding how to use the packet table. Please make the main thing you prepare that sign, but only if Lena confirms that every seed packet has a lot label. I don't know whether she has confirmed it yet, so don't assume that she has.

If she has confirmed every packet is labeled, write the sign. If she has not confirmed that, or if she says even one packet does not have a lot label, don't write the sign yet. In that case give me a concise checklist of the label information the organizers need to confirm or collect before the sign can be written. The point of the checklist is to help Lena and Dev check the packets, not to describe what a finished sign might say. Please give just one of those two things according to the condition, not the sign and checklist together. Don't decide on your own that the condition is met.

For the sign branch, keep it between 250 and 350 words so it can fit on one letter-size, 8.5 by 11 inch sheet. Make it readable at a table, with a clear heading and short numbered sections if that works. I was thinking three sections: how the exchange works, choosing packets, and leaving extras, though you can arrange those points so the instructions make sense. It should sound welcoming and practical, not like official rules or a gardening lecture. The sign is for a neighborhood event, and people may be new to seed exchanges, so explain the basic steps plainly without assuming they know the routine.

The exchange has packets from 14 local growers. Packets received include Scarlet Runner Bean, Moon and Stars watermelon, and Lacinato kale; those are examples from what came in, not a promise that all three will still be there when someone reads the sign. Please don't turn the examples into a complete inventory or say that a particular variety is available. People may bring seeds to share, but they can also take packets if they didn't bring any. Each visitor may take up to three packets. Don't suggest that visitors have to donate seeds, register, or pay. Nobody is expected to take three, either.

For the sign, explain that people can browse the packets and choose up to three, then leave any unopened packets they decide not to take on the table. The volunteers are going to count the unopened extras after the exchange. Lena said, “Please leave the unopened packets on the blue cloth so we can count them after the exchange.” Keep that instruction and the blue cloth detail in the sign if you write it; don't recast the quote as a rule about every packet or imply that opened packets should be returned. It should be clear that the blue cloth is where people leave the unopened extras, not where they have to put packets they are taking.

A lot label on each packet is the condition for writing the sign. For this exchange, a complete lot label has the crop name, variety name, harvest year, grower initials, and growing notes. By growing notes I mean the short notes printed on that packet, such as sun or spacing information when the grower supplied it; don't add growing information that isn't on a label. If the sign branch applies, tell visitors to use the label to identify the seeds and read the notes, but don't interpret the notes for them or promise anything about germination, yield, or how well a plant will grow. We don't have test results or guarantees to cite.

For the checklist branch, list those five label fields so Lena and Dev can check what is present on the packets: crop name, variety name, harvest year, grower initials, and growing notes. Make the checklist short and usable while they are standing at the table. It should let them identify whether all packets have the complete lot label, and make clear that an unconfirmed label or a missing field means the sign isn't ready. Don't add other document checks or ask them to collect information unrelated to those five fields. The sign is delayed only by the label check; the checklist isn't a replacement sign.

The hall's south entrance is on Alder Street, and the packet table is inside near the entrance. Visitors do not need to check in before browsing. Keep those practical details in mind if you refer to the location or arrival process, and don't invent a different entrance, room, or check-in desk. There will be pencils on the table, but there isn't a separate registration sheet. If a short location detail helps people find the table, the south entrance and the nearby table are the useful facts; we don't need directions from across town.

The sign should not say that every packet has been inspected unless Lena has actually confirmed it, and the only trigger I'm giving you is her confirmation that every packet has a complete lot label. If she says she's still checking, use the checklist branch. If she confirms all labels, use the sign branch and don't include a caveat that labels might be incomplete. Don't add event outcomes, endorsements, approval language, or a summary after the selected item.
